session.question: How was ARDL used to test the nexus, and what long-run association did it reveal for human capital and renewable energy?
session.answer:
The nexus was tested using an autoregressive distributed lag framework, specifically a cross-sectionally augmented ARDL (CS-ARDL) model in one study and standard ARDL bounds testing in another. The ARDL approach was applied within the load capacity curve or sustainability framework to estimate both short-run and long-run dynamics after preliminary stationarity testing where relevant. This setup is designed to handle heterogeneity, endogeneity, fractional integration, and cross-sectional dependence in panel data, while also identifying the long-run cointegration relationship among the variables. (dai2023assessingthenexus chunk 1, huang2021agatewaytowards chunk 1, zhu2022theroleof chunk 1)

In terms of long-run effects, the results consistently show a favorable association for human capital and renewable/green energy. Human capital was found to expand the load capacity factor and improve environmental quality, while green energy also increased the load capacity factor, indicating a positive contribution to sustainability in the long run. Similarly, in emerging economies, human capital and green energy reduced environmental degradation and carbon emissions in both the short and long run, implying a negative long-run association with emissions. Overall, the evidence indicates that human capital and renewable energy support environmental sustainability over the long run. (dai2023assessingthenexus chunk 1, huang2021agatewaytowards chunk 1, zhu2022theroleof chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-5058dbfb: The study used a cross-sectionally augmented ARDL (CS-ARDL) model, designed to be robust to heterogeneity, fractional integration, endogeneity, and cross-sectional dependence, to examine the relationship between human capital, green energy, and the load capacity factor in ASEAN countries from 1986–2018. The ARDL analysis was applied within the load capacity curve (LCC) framework to test both short- and long-run dynamics. Results showed a positive long-run association: human capital expands the load capacity factor and improves environmental quality, and green/renewable energy also stimulates the load capacity factor, supporting the idea that both variables contribute to sustainability in the long run.
From Jiapeng Dai, Zahoor Ahmed, Rafael Alvarado, and Mahmood Ahmad. Assessing the nexus between human capital, green energy, and load capacity factor: policymaking for achieving sustainable development goals. Gondwana Research, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gr.2023.04.009, doi:10.1016/j.gr.2023.04.009.

pqac-ae881b04: The study used a Cross-Sectionally Augmented ARDL (CS-ARDL) approach to examine the nexus between human capital index, green energy, economic growth (GDP and GDP squared), and carbon emissions in emerging economies using data from 1995–2018. The abstract says the CS-ARDL results showed that economic growth was the main driver of higher carbon emissions in both the short and long run. In contrast, human capital and green energy had a constructive effect in reducing environmental degradation in both long-run and short-run estimations, indicating a negative association with carbon emissions in the long run.
From Shi‐Zheng Huang, Fengsheng Chien, and Muhammad Sadiq. A gateway towards a sustainable environment in emerging countries: the nexus between green energy and human capital. Economic Research-Ekonomska Istraživanja, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1080/1331677x.2021.2012218, doi:10.1080/1331677x.2021.2012218.

pqac-86718174: The study used an advanced panel technique, cross-sectionally augmented distributed lags (CS-ARDL), to examine long-run and short-run relationships among green technologies, clean energy, environmental taxes, foreign investment, environmental sustainability, and human well-being in the top eight advanced economies from 1990 to 2018. The CS-ARDL estimation confirmed that green technologies have a positive effect on environmental and human well-being by reducing haze pollution and promoting human development. It also found that clean energy (renewable energy) contributes to a sustainable environment and human development in the long run, indicating a positive long-run association with human capital development.
From Nguyen Binh An, Yen-Lin Kuo, Fatma Mabrouk, Shouvik Sanyal, Iskandar Muda, Sanil S. Hishan, and Niamat Abdulrehman. Ecological innovation for environmental sustainability and human capital development: the role of environmental regulations and renewable energy in advanced economies. Economic Research-Ekonomska Istraživanja, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1080/1331677x.2022.2120046, doi:10.1080/1331677x.2022.2120046.

pqac-d8bcf5b3: The paper used an autoregressive distributed lag model (ARDL) to test the relationship (nexus) among the variables after checking stationarity with the augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test. According to the abstract, the ARDL results showed that human capital, renewable energy consumption, and renewable energy production were negatively associated with carbon emissions and positively associated with sustainable development goals (SDG). This indicates a favorable long-run association of human capital and renewable energy with SDG, while they help reduce carbon emissions. The study used Chinese data from 1986 to 2019 based on World Development Indicators.
From Mingqi Zhu. The role of human capital and environmental protection on the sustainable development goals: new evidences from chinese economy. Economic Research-Ekonomska Istraživanja, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1080/1331677x.2022.2113334, doi:10.1080/1331677x.2022.2113334.

pqac-f7ebab35: The paper used a time-series methodology on Bangladesh data from 1980–2019. It first applied the autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) bounds testing approach to examine the long-run nexus among carbon emissions, economic growth, renewable energy use, and technological innovation, and then used Dynamic Ordinary Least Squares (DOLS) for long-run coefficient estimation. The abstract reports that renewable energy use has a negative and significant long-run coefficient: a 1% increase in renewable energy use is associated with a 0.15% reduction in CO2 emissions. It also notes technological innovation is negative but not significant. The excerpt does not mention human capital.
From Asif Raihan, Dewan Ahmed Muhtasim, Md. Nafiul Alam Khan, Monirul Islam Pavel, and Omar Faruk. Nexus between carbon emissions, economic growth, renewable energy use, and technological innovation towards achieving environmental sustainability in bangladesh. Cleaner Energy Systems, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cles.2022.100032, doi:10.1016/j.cles.2022.100032.

session.formatted_answer:
Question: How was ARDL used to test the nexus, and what long-run association did it reveal for human capital and renewable energy?

The nexus was tested using an autoregressive distributed lag framework, specifically a cross-sectionally augmented ARDL (CS-ARDL) model in one study and standard ARDL bounds testing in another. The ARDL approach was applied within the load capacity curve or sustainability framework to estimate both short-run and long-run dynamics after preliminary stationarity testing where relevant. This setup is designed to handle heterogeneity, endogeneity, fractional integration, and cross-sectional dependence in panel data, while also identifying the long-run cointegration relationship among the variables. (dai2023assessingthenexus chunk 1, huang2021agatewaytowards chunk 1, zhu2022theroleof chunk 1)

In terms of long-run effects, the results consistently show a favorable association for human capital and renewable/green energy. Human capital was found to expand the load capacity factor and improve environmental quality, while green energy also increased the load capacity factor, indicating a positive contribution to sustainability in the long run. Similarly, in emerging economies, human capital and green energy reduced environmental degradation and carbon emissions in both the short and long run, implying a negative long-run association with emissions. Overall, the evidence indicates that human capital and renewable energy support environmental sustainability over the long run. (dai2023assessingthenexus chunk 1, huang2021agatewaytowards chunk 1, zhu2022theroleof chunk 1)
